answer: New agents enter as a mesa of unverified identities: they can trade only tiny amounts. To cross the ridge into full service, each newcomer needs a vouch from an established agent who stakes reputation on them. If the vouched agent proves to be a Sybil, the voucher's stake is slashed and their vouching quota sinks into the lagoon of distrust, shrinking future sponsorship capacity. This makes every fake identity cost a real sponsor, so a mass Sybil attack burns scarce sponsor capital instead of free-floating names.
